description: Fungal disease causing dark brown spots with concentric rings on lower leaves, leading to defoliation and reduced fruit production.
symptoms: Dark brown to black lesions on lower leaves
Concentric rings forming target-like pattern
Yellowing around spots (chlorosis)
Leaf defoliation in severe cases
Stem cankers near ground level
causes: High humidity or extended leaf wetness
spread_methods: Water splashes from rain or irrigation

environmental_factors.optimal_conditions: Warm, humid weather with poor air circulation

severity_levels.mild: <10% leaf area affected with scattered spots
severity_levels.moderate: 10-30% leaf area affected with coalescing lesions
severity_levels.severe: >30% leaf area affected with extensive defoliation

description: Devastating oomycete disease causing water-soaked lesions that rapidly expand and destroy entire plants.
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems
White fungal growth on undersides of leaves in humid conditions
Dark brown to black lesions on stems
Firm, brown lesions on fruits
Rapid plant death in favorable conditions
spread_methods: Spores spread by wind and rain

environmental_factors.optimal_conditions: Cool, wet weather with extended leaf wetness

severity_levels.moderate: Expanding lesions with some plant tissue death
severity_levels.severe: Extensive lesions leading to plant death

description: Fungal disease causing small circular spots with dark borders and gray centers on lower leaves.
symptoms: Small circular spots (2-3mm) on lower leaves
Dark brown borders with grayish-white centers
Black fruiting bodies visible in spot centers
Yellowing and death of affected leaves
Progression from bottom to top of plant

severity_levels.severe: Extensive spotting leading to severe defoliation

description: Devastating disease responsible for Irish potato famine, causing rapid destruction of foliage and tubers.
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems
White fungal growth on leaf undersides
Dark brown lesions on tubers
Rapid plant collapse in favorable conditions
Dry, firm rot in stored tubers

severity_levels.moderate: Expanding lesions with some plant death
severity_levels.severe: Complete foliage destruction and tuber infection

description: Fungal disease causing dark brown lesions with concentric rings on leaves and tubers.
symptoms: Dark brown lesions with target-like pattern on lower leaves
Leaf yellowing and premature death
Dark, sunken lesions on tubers
Reduced yield and tuber quality
spread_methods: Conidia spread by wind and rain

severity_levels.moderate: Moderate leaf damage with some defoliation
severity_levels.severe: Extensive leaf death and tuber infection

description: Fungal disease causing olive-green to black lesions on leaves, fruit, and twigs, affecting fruit quality.
symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety lesions on leaves
Scabby lesions on fruit surface
Cracked and distorted fruit
Twig dieback in severe cases
Reduced fruit quality and marketability
causes: Dormant fungal spores in bark and fallen leaves

severity_levels.mild: Isolated spots on leaves and fruit
severity_levels.severe: Extensive infection causing fruit deformities and yield loss

description: Bacterial disease causing blossom blight, shoot dieback, and cankers that can kill entire trees.
symptoms: Water-soaked blossom wilting and blackening
Shepherd's crook on new shoots
Sunken cankers with bacterial ooze
Shoot dieback and tree death
Burned appearance of affected areas

severity_levels.moderate: Limited shoot infection with some dieback
severity_levels.severe: Extensive infection leading to tree death

description: Fungal disease causing white to grayish cottony growth on leaves and fruit, affecting photosynthesis and quality.
symptoms: White to grayish cottony growth on lower leaf surfaces
Yellowing and curling of leaves
Reduced fruit quality and yield
In severe cases, defoliation and fruit rot
causes: Cool wet weather with high humidity
Poor air circulation in dense canopies
Infected plant debris from previous season

environmental_factors.susceptible_stages: All growth stages, especially young leaves
environmental_factors.optimal_conditions: Cool, wet weather with poor air circulation

severity_levels.mild: Sparse mildew growth on isolated leaves
severity_levels.severe: Complete leaf coverage with defoliation and fruit infection

description: Bacterial disease causing yellowing of leaves, green discoloration of fruit, and premature fruit drop.
symptoms: Yellow mottling of leaves with distinct veins
Green spots and blotches on fruit rind
Bitter taste and misshapen fruit
Premature fruit drop and reduced yield
spread_methods: Tool contamination during pruning and grafting

severity_levels.mild: Leaf yellowing with minimal fruit impact
severity_levels.moderate: Extensive leaf yellowing with some fruit greening
severity_levels.severe: Severe defoliation with widespread fruit infection

description: Fungal disease causing rectangular gray lesions on leaves that can reduce photosynthesis and yield.
symptoms: Gray to tan rectangular lesions on leaves
Lesions with distinct borders and yellow halos
Lesion coalescence in severe infections
Premature leaf death and reduced yield
Stalk breakage in severe cases
causes: High humidity and extended leaf wetness

environmental_factors.optimal_conditions: Warm, humid weather during active growth

severity_levels.mild: Few scattered lesions on lower leaves
severity_levels.moderate: Numerous lesions causing moderate leaf damage
severity_levels.severe: Extensive lesions leading to significant yield loss

description: Fungal disease causing white powdery growth on leaves, stems, and heads, reducing photosynthesis and grain quality.
symptoms: White to gray powdery patches on leaves and stems
Yellowing and stunting of affected tissue
Reduced grain quality and yield
Severe infection leads to head damage and grain loss
causes: Dry conditions favor spore production and spread

environmental_factors.optimal_conditions: Cool temperatures with high humidity and cloudy conditions

severity_levels.mild: Scattered powdery growth on lower leaves
severity_levels.moderate: Widespread powdery mildew on multiple leaves
severity_levels.severe: Complete leaf coverage with stem and head infection

description: Devastating fungal disease causing rapid wilting, leaf scorch, and plant death without warning signs.
symptoms: Rapid wilting and death of infected plants
Interveinal chlorosis and necrosis
Brown to black discoloration of lower stem and root cortex
White cottony fungal growth on stem in humid conditions
Premature plant death before flowering

environmental_factors.susceptible_stages: All vegetative stages, especially V2-V4 stage
environmental_factors.optimal_conditions: Warm, moist soil conditions with plant stress

severity_levels.moderate: Patches of affected plants with moderate symptoms

description: Complex disease causing rotting of cotton bolls during maturation, reducing lint quality and yield.
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on developing bolls
External rot and fungal growth on bolls
Internal rot with discolored lint
Premature boll opening and shedding
Reduced lint quality and weight
causes: Excess nitrogen and late application of irrigation
Boll injury from insects or weather
spread_methods: Water splash and contaminated irrigation water

environmental_factors.optimal_conditions: Warm, humid weather during boll development

severity_levels.moderate: Multiple affected bolls with significant yield loss
severity_levels.severe: Widespread boll infection with >50% boll loss

description: Fungal disease causing white powdery growth on leaves, flowers, and fruit, affecting photosynthesis and market quality.
symptoms: White powdery patches on upper leaf surfaces
Leaf curling and stunting
White fungal growth on flowers and fruit
Reduced fruit quality and yield
Severe infections lead to fruit deformities
causes: High humidity and poor air circulation

environmental_factors.susceptible_stages: All growth stages, especially flowering and fruiting
environmental_factors.optimal_conditions: Moderate temperatures with high humidity and cloudy conditions

severity_levels.mild: Scattered powdery growth on isolated leaves
severity_levels.severe: Complete leaf coverage with severe fruit infection

description: Fungal disease causing white downy growth on leaves, reducing photosynthesis and market quality.
symptoms: White downy growth on lower leaf surfaces
Yellowing and leaf curling
Stunted plant growth
Reduced head quality and yield
causes: High humidity and poor air circulation
spread_methods: Spores dispersed by wind and rain

environmental_factors.optimal_conditions: Cool, wet weather with dense canopy

severity_levels.severe: Complete leaf coverage with severe head quality reduction

description: Complex disease causing head rot with watery decay and foul odor, rendering crops unmarketable.
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on head and curd
Slimy, foul-smelling decay of affected tissue
Gray to black discoloration of affected areas
Premature rotting before harvest maturity
Complete head loss in severe cases
causes: Poor air circulation and high humidity
Physical damage during cultivation and harvest

severity_levels.mild: Isolated rot spots on few heads
severity_levels.moderate: Multiple heads affected with partial rot

description: Bacterial disease causing water-soaked lesions that become translucent and yellow, reducing photosynthesis and yield.
symptoms: Water-soaked, angular lesions on leaves
Lesions turning yellow, brown, and translucent
Leaf death in severe infections
Reduced tillering and grain production
causes: Rain splash dispersal during monsoon rains
spread_methods: Soil-borne survival in weeds and crop residue

severity_levels.severe: Widespread infection with >50% leaf damage and yield loss

description: Fungal disease causing dark brown to black lesions with concentric rings on carrot leaves and petioles.
symptoms: Dark brown to black lesions with concentric rings
Leaf yellowing and death from petioles inward
Reduced photosynthesis and plant growth
lesions on carrot roots and crowns in severe cases
causes: Poor soil drainage and nutrient imbalances
spread_methods: Conidia spread by wind and rain

environmental_factors.susceptible_stages: All growth stages, especially mature foliage
environmental_factors.optimal_conditions: Warm, humid weather with poor air circulation

severity_levels.moderate: Multiple lesions with some leaf loss
severity_levels.severe: Extensive infection causing significant yield loss
